tasks.title: Numbered list
tasks.statement: Print the names from the list with numbers starting at one, in the form «1. Ann». Use enumerate with the start parameter.
tasks.hint: for i, name in enumerate(names, start=1): print(f"{i}. {name}").

tasks.title: Where the maximum is
tasks.statement: Write a function index_of_max(nums): the index of the largest element of a non-empty list. If there are several largest elements, return the index of the first one. It is convenient to loop with enumerate.
tasks.hint: Compare strictly: if x > nums[best_i]: best_i = i. Then on a tie the first one stays.

tasks.title: Pairwise sums
tasks.statement: Write a function pair_sums(a, b): a new list whose i-th element is the sum of a[i] and b[i]. The lists have the same length. Pair them up with zip.
tasks.hint: for x, y in zip(a, b): result.append(x + y).

tasks.title: Every other one
tasks.statement: Write a function interleave(a, b): a list in which the elements of two lists (of the same length) alternate: a[0], b[0], a[1], b[1] and so on.
tasks.hint: On every pass of zip, two appends: first x, then y.

tasks.hint: for row in matrix: for x in row: result.append(x), or result.extend(row).

tasks.title: Remove the negatives
tasks.statement: Write a function drop_negatives(nums): the list without negative numbers (zero stays). Do not delete elements from the list you are looping over: consecutive negatives get skipped that way. Build a new list.
